_: Prot name vocabulary. The names are build-agnostic - only the opcode NUMBERS move, so every opcode->name map is filed under the build it was derived from and is invalid for any other build. PROVENANCE MATTERS: neither client binary contains prot names at all (the stripped target has no prot-name strings; jag::ServerProt in the unstripped reference is a class, not a named enum), so every name here came from OUTSIDE the binaries - the legacy Project X ServerPacket enum and community naming - or was invented here. Names listed in assigned_names are INVENTED PLACEHOLDERS, not Jagex names: never promote them, never tag them OFFICIAL_PROT_NAME, and never give a sibling handler a version-style suffix (_V2/_V3/_2) that reads as Jagex versioning. Use _ALT.  CORRECTION (950-1): there are TWO attestation sources, and consulting only this file's official_names list caused 37 genuinely Jagex-attested names to be mis-filed as invented. re-resources/updater/official_prot_names.json carries the jag::ServerProt / jag::ClientProt / jag::ZoneProt SYMBOL names from an unstripped BETA client (NXT_BETA_UNSTRIPPED) - 295 names, and that is Jagex's own naming, not community naming. It does not contradict the statement above: the two binaries we work with daily (the stripped target and the modern unstripped reference) genuinely carry no prot names; the beta build did. ALWAYS check both files before filing a name as assigned. A name absent from both is still a placeholder.

_zone_notes.949-5.6: Adjudicated from the handler bodies, not by elimination: 949-5 carried TWO distinct functions both named jag::PacketHandlers::MapAnim, and both carried the same copied decompiler comment, so the comments were not independent evidence. The 237-instruction handler resolves the tile through LinkMap::ReadTileFlags, keeps a persistent tile-keyed entry in the zone location container, treats an id of -1 as a clear-and-free, and is LOC_ANIM. The 127-instruction handler does no LinkMap lookup, keeps no container entry, has no clear path, and simply spawns at the tile height - that is MAP_ANIM. Named-call sets separate them cleanly and the reading holds independently in both builds. ⛔ CONTESTED at 950-1: this 949-5 assignment came from the same LocAnim/MapAnim symbol confusion that was later retracted on the new build. The body argument used here (LinkMap resolve, tile-keyed container entry, -1 clear) was never re-checked against the ApplyLocChange/record-kind evidence that identified the real LOC_ANIM on 950-1. Re-verify before relying on the 949-5 zone names for anything.
_zone_notes.949-5.1: Left UNKNOWN deliberately. Three weak signals point at LOC_ADD - the live rev949 codec maps LocAdd to this sub-opcode, the handler sits immediately above the confirmed LocDel handler in .text, and the size is varByte which matches how the codec registers LocAdd - but the same codec was wrong on three of its twelve mappings, and address adjacency is not identity. Confirm it from the handler body (it should insert a Location into the zone container the way LOC_ANIM does, without the animation drive) before naming it. Carries to 950-1 sub 8.
_zone_notes.949-5.2: Unnamed in both builds (a thunk in 949-5). No external attestation exists for it. Carries to 950-1 sub 7.

_provenance.950-1: Opcodes and sizes are read structurally from rs2client.950-1 by RS3ProtFinder (registration walk, no names involved). Names are carried from the 949-5 map by HANDLER FUNCTION IDENTITY - never by opcode number, which is fully re-scrambled on a major bump - using the old->new function map from the migration. Packet size is invariant across this bump (114 of 115 carried handler names keep an identical size; the sole exception is UPDATE_STOCKMARKET_SLOT, 35 -> 36), so a size mismatch was treated as disqualifying. Four zone sub-packets were removed (the non-Big OBJ_ADD/OBJ_DEL/OBJ_REVEAL/OBJ_COUNT) and three interface handlers (IF_SETOBJECT, IF_SETOBJECT_LONG, IF_OPENSUB_ACTIVE_OBJ). FIELD LAYOUTS CHANGED WIDELY EVEN AT UNCHANGED SIZE - no encoder or decoder body may be ported; every one must be re-derived from this build.
_provenance.950-1.corrections: Nine opcode->name bindings were corrected after the codec rebuild re-derived the opcode<->handler map STRUCTURALLY from the new binary (ServerProt::RegisterAll's 223 InitEntry calls and ZoneProt::InitSubEntry's 18, joined against the four binder functions that store each handler at entry+0x28) rather than by carrying names through function identity. Zero size disagreements against the earlier table. The most consequential: SERVER 14 is LOC_ANIM, not MAP_ANIM - MAP_ANIM exists only as a zone sub-opcode and has no standalone opcode on this build. UPDATE_STAT was missed by the earlier join because it binds as jag::game::StatTable::UpdateStat rather than under jag::PacketHandlers::.
_provenance.name_filing_correction: Merged the 295 unstripped-beta symbol names into official_names and removed 37 of them from assigned_names, where this migration had wrongly filed them: CLIENT_CHEAT, EVENT_CAMERA_POSITION, EVENT_KEYBOARD, IF_BUTTONT, MOVE_MINIMAPCLICK, OPLOC1, OPLOC2, OPLOC3, OPLOC4, OPLOC5, OPLOC6, OPLOCT, OPNPC1, OPNPC2, OPNPC3, OPNPC4, OPNPC5, OPNPC6, OPNPCT, OPOBJ1, OPOBJ2, OPOBJ3, OPOBJ4, OPOBJ5, OPOBJ6, OPOBJT, OPPLAYER1, OPPLAYER10, OPPLAYER2, OPPLAYER3, OPPLAYER4, OPPLAYER5, OPPLAYER6, OPPLAYER7, OPPLAYER8, OPPLAYER9, STORE_SERVERPERM_VARCS. This reverses a mis-filing made during this migration, not a pre-existing one, and it is not a promotion of an invented name - the names were always attested and were recorded as assigned only because the check consulted one authority file instead of two. 72 further attested names were absent from official_names entirely and are now included.
_provenance.950-1.loc_anim_retraction: SERVER 14 was recorded as LOC_ANIM on the strength of the Ghidra symbol on its bound handler. That symbol is mis-migrated and the correction is RETRACTED: read adversarially, the handler resolves no Location at all - no shape/rotation decode, no loc-change record, no ApplyLocChange - and places a free-standing scene node at the tile centre by fine coordinate, removing by walking the node list on fine X/Y, where the real loc path is keyed by packed tile and shape layer. It is byte-for-byte MAP_ANIM_ALT's handler minus the trailing fine offset. It is an unidentified third sibling and stays UNKNOWN_14; naming it would be invention, since MAP_ANIM is taken and MAP_ANIM_ALT is itself an assigned name. The half of the original correction that stands is that the table's MAP_ANIM at SERVER 14 was also wrong - MAP_ANIM exists only as a zone sub-opcode. The real LOC_ANIM is SERVER 11 / ZONE 8 on three independent lines: it calls the loc shape/rotation decoder and ApplyLocChange; the loc-change record's kind field partitions the four zone loc handlers onto the four LOC_* prots with no slot left over; and decisively it writes its id to the record's ANIMATION slot while forcing the TYPE slot to -1, i.e. it animates an existing loc rather than changing its type, which is the inverse of LOC_ADD_CHANGE. SERVER 104 / ZONE 7 is the kind-4 handler reading recolour/retexture arrays: LOC_CUSTOMISE. Both names are attested in the unstripped-beta symbol set.
_provenance.950-1.friendlist_del: The CLIENT opcode our previous codec bound to FRIENDLIST_DEL does not delete a friend, and the same is true of the 950-1 slot the carried table put the name on (CLIENT 74). Its descriptor has exactly two referrers besides RegisterAll, both CS2 opcode handlers: one pops a string, refuses to send when it is empty and prints a localized 'The channel you tried to join does not exist.', while the other takes no argument and sends a single zero byte. That is a join/leave pair on one opcode - a length byte counting the NUL where zero means leave, followed by a CP1252 channel name. The 949-5 counterpart (CLIENT 63, joined by function identity) has the identical body and string, so the 949 binding was wrong too and FRIENDLIST_DEL was never decoded on either build. The opcode is left UNKNOWN_74 deliberately: the only attested name of that shape is CLAN_JOINCHAT_LEAVECHAT, but the binary says 'channel' without separating a clan channel from a friends-chat channel, and that distinction is exactly what would have to be proven. FRIENDLIST_DEL itself remains attested and unused on this build.
_provenance.950-1.lobby_tick_end: LOBBY_TICK_END is SERVER 183: the size-0 entry bound in ServerProt::BindHandlers at the same binder position as 949-5's SERVER 140, the only size-0 slot that aligns, with the same two-instruction no-op body. The identity rests on binder order plus the unique size, because a no-op body carries no signature and the packet is unfalsifiable from captures; the name stays an assigned placeholder carried from 949 (not attested). Supersedes the earlier note that found no opcode.
_provenance.950-1.if_setobject_long: SERVER 173 (size 15) is the interface-component object setter with a 64-bit count: entry kind 0x16, the object id in the entry slot, the count written as a qword tagged int64, then the same ObjType seeding IF_SETOBJECT performs. The 949 handler is gone, but this is the packet 949's assigned name IF_SETOBJECT_LONG denoted, so the name carries onto 173 as an assigned name; it is not attested. SERVER 118 is refuted for that role (component head/model source, sub-kind 7, no ObjType load). Supersedes the earlier admitted-gap note.
_provenance.950-1.server_221_transform: SERVER 221 (a global entity render-mode flag) changed its wire transform silently: the previous build read it as an add-byte, this build reads it raw, so anything still emitting the add form lands 128 off. We do not encode it, so we are unaffected - recorded because it is exactly the class of change an unchanged packet SIZE would hide.
_provenance.950-1.unbound_entries: SERVER 57 and 158 register an opcode and a size but no binder ever stores a handler, so the client frames the packet and discards it. Confirmed by the structural registration walk, not inferred from a missing name.
_provenance.950-1.if_buttond: CLIENT 12 (size 18) is IF_BUTTOND. On 949-5 jag::InterfaceManager::SendIfButtonD emitted two packets - the current 18-byte drag form the table called IF_DRAG and, behind a pre-949 revision gate, a legacy 16-byte form the table called IF_BUTTOND. On 950-1 the gate and the legacy descriptor are gone: the same function references exactly one descriptor and has exactly one send, so the attested name IF_BUTTOND names the only drag packet and the assigned placeholder IF_DRAG retires. There is no 16-byte ClientProt on 950-1.
_provenance.950-1.structural_join: Every 950-1 ServerProt (223) and ZoneProt (18) entry was joined to its 949-5 handler by function identity: the migration function map first, then binder-source-order plus exact-registered-size alignment between the paired binder functions scored by normalized-disassembly similarity and confirmed by wildcarded byte signatures of the 949-5 body. Opcode and size read from the 950-1 registration walk agree with this table on all 241 rows. Blind, the alignment disagreed with the function-map ground truth on 0 of 91 pairs. Two SERVER opcodes are new (74, 116: varByte handlers in the varc binder with no 949-5 counterpart), two register but never bind (57, 158), and eight 949-5 handlers are gone: OBJ_ADD, OBJ_DEL, OBJ_REVEAL, OBJ_COUNT (the small variants), IF_SETOBJECT's 949 handler, IF_SETOBJECT_LONG, IF_OPENSUB_ACTIVE_OBJ's 949 handler, and 949 UNKNOWN_174.
_provenance.950-1.map_anim: SERVER 14 / ZONE 11 is MAP_ANIM. Its handler is 949-5's jag::PacketHandlers::MapAnim (949 SERVER 173 / zone sub 6) by the migration function map with 0.966 body similarity, 237 instructions in both, same binder position, size 11 - the handler whose packet the live 949 servers used for tile graphics in every capture. Its 14-byte sibling in the same binder is MAP_ANIM_ALT, which is the sibling relationship the earlier retraction observed. The other 11-byte tile-graphic handler, bound zone-only at ZONE 1, is 949-5's zone-only sub 15, which no 949 table ever named, so ZONE 1 is UNKNOWN_1 rather than MAP_ANIM. This supersedes the half of 950-1.loc_anim_retraction that left SERVER 14 unnamed; the LOC_ANIM = SERVER 11 / ZONE 8 finding stands.
_provenance.950-1.obj_official_names: 950-1 keeps exactly one handler per ground-item operation: the 949-5 functions previously labelled ObjAddBig, ObjCountBig, ObjDelBig and ObjRevealBig, joined by function identity (binder order, size, migration map for OBJ_COUNT, byte signatures for OBJ_DEL). With the small 949 variants removed there is nothing left for the attested names OBJ_ADD, OBJ_COUNT, OBJ_DEL and OBJ_REVEAL to denote except these, so SERVER 51 / ZONE 0 is OBJ_ADD, SERVER 70 / ZONE 6 is OBJ_COUNT, SERVER 109 / ZONE 10 is OBJ_DEL and ZONE 9 is OBJ_REVEAL; the assigned *_BIG placeholders retire on this build.
_provenance.950-1.invented_names_retired: MISC_NEW_945 (SERVER 214), MISC_NEW_946 (141), NEW_AUDIO945 (211) and UNNAMED_1 (170) are the 949-5 handlers by function identity (0.97, 0.97, 0.98 and 0.60 body similarity) but none of those names is attested and none can be proven by behaviour: 214 is a zero-payload teardown plus deadline re-arm, 141 a clock/latency sync (SEND_PING is independently SERVER 190), 211 an audio-manager dispatch that was assigned by elimination, 170 a one-byte discriminator plus string. They are UNKNOWN_<op> on this build.
_provenance.950-1.zone_14_binder_defect: ZONE 14 is registered with TEXT_COORD's varByte size but BindZoneHandlers copies the LOC_PREFETCH delegate into it (the copy reads the neighbouring entry); 949-5 has the identical defect. A TEXT_COORD sent inside a zone bundle runs the loc-prefetch handler on this client.
_provenance.950-1.behaviour_confirmations: Names 950-1 assigned by behaviour were re-derived independently from the handler bodies: CONFIRMED LOC_ANIM (11, loc record kind 2, animation slot set, type slot -1, ApplyLocChange), IF_OPENSUB_ACTIVE_PLAYER (13, indexes the player array), IF_SETPLAYERMODEL_OTHER (37, component property sub-kind 5 with a 16-bit player id), IF_OPENSUB_ACTIVE_NPC (42, NPCList::GetNPCNode), IF_MOVESUB (45, detaches and re-registers the open sub), IF_SETANIM (47, model property kind 5, releases the built model), IF_SETPLAYERHEAD_OTHER (59, sub-kind 3 with a 16-bit id), IF_SETANGLE (68, entry kind 8 seeded by IF_SETOBJECT from the ObjType render fields), IF_OPENSUB_ACTIVE_OBJ (91, ground-obj list lookup), IF_SETOBJECT (102, entry kind 9 then ObjType seeding), LOC_CUSTOMISE (104, record kind 4 with recolour and retexture arrays), IF_SETRECOL (150, first recolour pair), IF_SETRETEX (168, second pair, releases the model), OBJ_ADD/OBJ_COUNT/OBJ_DEL/OBJ_REVEAL (51/70/109/zone 9: insert, count rewrite where id and old count match, erase, insert skipped when the owner is the local player). NOT PROVEN and therefore UNKNOWN: 39 (writes one int to a component field with no update entry; IF_SETGRAPHIC, IF_SETCLICKMASK and IF_SETTEXTFONT fit equally) and 128 (a create-account status reply placed only by elimination against 137). VARP_LONG (165) and CLIENT_SETVARC_LONG (200) are behaviour-proven 64-bit variants of packets the reference client only has in 32-bit form; they are assigned names for packets newer than the reference, not attested.
_provenance.950-1.set_moveaction: SET_MOVEACTION (123, varByte): a payload of at least three bytes is a NUL-terminated CP1252 op text followed by a g2 cursor id (0xffff = none); an EMPTY payload is a first-class path that resets the text to the localised default ('Walk here') and the cursor to none. Lengths 1 and 2 still perform the two-byte read and over-run, so a server emits only 0 or >= 3.
_provenance.950-1.lobby_tick_end.body: SERVER 183's bound handler is a two-instruction no-op that reads nothing; the fixed-length framing accepts the empty payload exactly as SERVER_TICK_END (160) does. Three byte-identical no-op stubs exist on this build (88, 172, 183) separable only by binder order and size.

_name_provenance_notes.LOBBY_TICK_END: Used by the rev949 codec in this repository but absent from official_names. Filed ASSIGNED because its provenance outside the binaries was not established during the 950-1 migration - not because it is known to be invented. Moving a name INTO official_names requires attestation; the reverse is never done.
_name_provenance_notes.IF_BUTTONT: Used by the rev949 codec in this repository but absent from official_names. It follows the IF_BUTTON1..10 family's naming shape and may well be attested, but that was not verified here, so it is filed ASSIGNED rather than asserted as official.
